title_en: Build ConfigManager as a singleton with __new__
spec_html_en: Write class ConfigManager using __new__ so that every call to ConfigManager() returns the exact same instance. __init__ is already implemented and only creates self.settings as an empty dict the first time, so re-running __init__ on later calls does not wipe existing state.
test:
def test_returns_same_instance():
    a = ConfigManager()
    b = ConfigManager()
    assert a is b, 'ConfigManager() must always return the same instance'

def test_shared_state_across_references():
    a = ConfigManager()
    a.settings['debug'] = True
    b = ConfigManager()
    assert b.settings['debug'] is True, 'all references must share the same underlying state'

def test_settings_not_reset_on_new_call():
    a = ConfigManager()
    a.settings['x'] = 1
    b = ConfigManager()
    assert b.settings['x'] == 1, 'creating a "new" instance must not wipe previously set state'
